search_intent: Chefs, caterers, and food handlers seeking strict commercial kitchen limits on how long cooked batch dishes, soups, roasted meats, rice, and pasta can be safely kept in refrigeration, the 2-day rule (day of prep + 2), and statutory 75°C single-reheat protocols.

competitors.title: Chilling Food Correctly | Food Standards Agency
competitors.strengths: Statutory UK authority on danger zone (8°C to 63°C).
competitors.weaknesses: Broad summary, lacks dish-by-dish commercial holding durations and printable kitchen charts.

competitors.title: How Long Can You Keep Leftovers? | BBC Good Food
competitors.weaknesses: Domestic consumer focus, lacks commercial catering 90-minute blast chilling mandate and EHO audit rules.

competitors.title: How Long Do Leftovers Really Last? | Healthline
competitors.weaknesses: General US consumer article, no commercial kitchen workflow or printable checklists.

competitors.title: Fridge Storage Times & Food Safety | High Speed Training
competitors.weaknesses: Static article, lacks interactive tool functionality.

competitors.title: FoodKeeper Storage Tool | FoodSafety.gov
competitors.weaknesses: Clunky mobile interface, US Fahrenheit focus, no commercial catering workflow.

gap_analysis.what_they_have: Domestic home tips or searchable lookup apps.
gap_analysis.what_they_lack: Commercial catering framework enforcing the 2-day rule, 90-minute cooling mandate, Bacillus cereus rice safety, single-reheat rules, and printable wall chart.
gap_analysis.what_we_offer: Interactive storage hierarchy tool with dish search, commercial blast-chilling protocols, statutory reheat limits (75°C core / 82°C Scotland), and instant A4 print layout.
